## Appeal Letter

Dear Meridian Health Insurance,

I am writing to appeal the denial of claim #CLM-2024-00891 for CPT 27447 (Total Knee Arthroplasty) denied on April 10, 2024. [S1]

The denial states prior authorization was not obtained; however, our records show authorization request #PA-2024-1823 was submitted on March 28, 2024. [S2]

Under California Insurance Code §10169.3, the insurer must respond to urgent prior authorization requests within 72 hours. [S3]

We respectfully request immediate reconsideration.

Sincerely,
Robert Chen

summary.explanation: Your knee replacement claim was denied because the insurer claims no prior authorization was on file. This is an administrative denial — the procedure itself is covered. Prior authorization disputes are often resolved quickly when you can demonstrate the authorization was requested or that the insurer failed to respond within the required timeframe.

rule_sources.text: Insurer must respond to prior authorization requests within 5 business days (or 72 hours for urgent cases).

S1.text: Services requiring prior authorization are listed in Schedule A. Total Knee Arthroplasty (CPT 27447) requires prior authorization.

S2.text: Authorization requests must be submitted via the provider portal or fax no less than 5 business days before the scheduled procedure.

S3.text: Insurer must respond to prior authorization requests within 5 business days (or 72 hours for urgent cases).
